newsitem.title: INDIA: India Finance Bill vote set for May 9.
newsitem.headline: India Finance Bill vote set for May 9.

text.p: India's lower house of parliament has scheduled a vote on the 1997/98 (April-March) Finance Bill for May 9, a parliamentary official said on Wednesday.
The Finance Bill, which includes the government's tax and tariff proposals, will be debated by the lower house, the Lok Sabha, on May 7, 8 and 9, the official said.
A vote is expected on May 9 at about 3 p.m. (0930 GMT), an aide to Parliamentary Affairs Minister Srikanta Jena told Reuters after a meeting of parliament's Business Advisory Committee.
Once approved by the lower house, the bill would be sent to the upper house, the Rajya Sabha, for ratification.

The aide said the Lok Sabha, which on Wednesday began a 2-1/2-week session on the budget, was set to discuss spending proposals in four areas -- human resource development, power, non-conventional energy resources and atomic energy -- on May 5 and 6.
There will be no debate on spending proposals in other areas for lack of time, he said.

Former finance minister P. Chidambaram presented the 1997/98 budget package to parliament on February 28. The package includes both the Finance Bill, which would cut corporate and personal income taxes, and the appropriations, or spending, proposals.

Chidambaram, who presented the budget under the previous government of ousted prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, was expected to be sworn in on Thursday as finance minister in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet.
Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) decided on Tuesday to join Gujral's nine-day-old government.
The party had earlier said it would stay out of the government after its leader G.K. Moopanar was passed over in the prime ministerial race.

Both leftwing parties in Gujral's United Front coalition and the Congress party have indicated they will not risk endangering the ruling alliance by proposing amendments to the Finance Bill on the floor of the house.
They have said they would discuss any proposed changes in advance with the government.
